Subject: Request: extra credits for nightly real-time soak

Diego —

Thanks again for the demo earlier this week. We validated the basic flows and are ready to run an aggressive nightly soak to validate 99th percentile latency under a real-time inference load. The soak will run for 8 nights (June 20–27), peak window 10pm–2am PST, simulating sustained 800 concurrent streams at 256 tokens/resp avg.

Request: can Redwood provision an additional temporary credit allocation for the soak (approx. 120k generation tokens/day, ~1M tokens total)? Also attaching our soak plan and baseline traces so you have the pattern (cloudscale-soak-plan.xlsx; soak-baseline-results.csv).

What we need from you:
- A promo/temporary credit or trial extension that covers the period (start June 20)
- A contact for any performance anomalies during the soak (on-call engineer)
- Confirmation of whether we should use hosted endpoints or reserve a short Dedicated pool for the window

We want to use this to finalize latency SLOs and decide whether to proceed with a 6-month pilot. Appreciate any flexibility here.

— Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Platform — CloudScale
ops@cloudscale.com

Thanks for the plan and the traces — helpful. Quick clarifications so I can route this for approval:

1) Confirm total token ask: you mentioned ~1M tokens total. Is that generation-only or tokens in+out?
2) Is the test synthetic traffic or replay of recorded user requests (we need to know if your load contains personally identifying data).
3) Any hard deadline tied to vendor procurement or RFP?

Marissa — looping you on the ask for a temporary credit/promo and the potential to reserve a short Dedicated pool if needed. Stephanie — can you advise whether an ephemeral dedicated instance is warranted for this traffic shape, or can the hosted pool with careful batching suffice?

My plan: once we confirm token math and PII status, I can approve a temporary credit up to $X and get Billing to issue a promo. If the customer prefers Dedicated we may need a short-term reservation and a nominal commit.

Diego

Samir —

Quick ops note from the SRE side: glad to support the soak. A couple of recommendations to reduce cost and keep latency tight:

- Use a shorter generation target per call where possible and stitch responses client-side (reduces variance in token cost spikes).
- Enable prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts (we can seed caches prior to the window).
- If you see tail-latency > 350ms consistently, request a Dedicated microlane for the 4-hour window — that will remove cross-tenant jitter.

I'll be on-call nights June 20–27. Please share the exact traffic generator command and credentials for the test harness (we'll whitelist the IPs).

— Rishi
